models.description:
# Model Summary

LoRA adapter for Brazilian crypto asset compliance reasoning, fine-tuned on **Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1** (46.7B parameters) via [Adaption's](https://adaptionlabs.ai) AutoScientist platform. Given a compliance query describing a crypto asset product, policy, or control gap, the model produces a structured JSON assessment with applicable regulations, risk level (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH), finding, and corrective action — covering **BCB · CVM · COAF** and federal legislation (Lei 14.478/2022, Decreto 11.563/2023).

Submitted to the **AutoScientist Challenge 2026** (Legal category).

## Usage

This is a LoRA adapter. Load it on top of the base model using the PEFT library:

```python
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1")

model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "Fernandosr85/regtech-br-legal-adapter")

prompt = """Analyze the following compliance question under Brazilian crypto asset regulation 
and produce a structured assessment:

Our exchange does not segregate client assets from our own funds. 
Do we need to comply with Brazilian regulations?"""

inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

**Input:** Natural language compliance query in Portuguese or English.  
**Output:** Structured JSON with `risk_level`, `compliance_status`, `applicable_regulations`, `relevant_articles`, `finding`, `corrective_action`, `confidence`, `authority`.

**Known limitations:** The model was fine-tuned on 19 examples covering Brazilian crypto regulation as of June 2026. Outputs should be reviewed by qualified legal professionals before any operational decision.

## System

Standalone LoRA adapter. Requires the base model `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` to be loaded first via PEFT. The adapter is deployed as part of the **RegTech BR** RAG pipeline ([HuggingFace Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Fernandosr85/regtech-br)), where a FAISS retriever provides regulatory context from 103 chunks of official BCB, CVM, COAF, and federal documents before inference.

## Implementation requirements

- **Training platform:** Adaption AutoScientist (cloud compute)
- **Base model size:** 46.7B parameters (Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1)
- **Training method:** SFT + LoRA (all-linear modules)
- **Training steps:** 69 steps · 3 epochs
- **Inference:** Requires GPU with sufficient VRAM to load Mixtral-8x7B (minimum ~48GB VRAM for full precision, or quantized variant)

---

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

Fine-tuned from `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` using LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation). The base model weights are frozen; only the LoRA adapter weights are trained.

## Model stats

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model | Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 |
| Base model size | 46.7B parameters |
| LoRA rank (r) | 32 |
| LoRA alpha | 64 |
| LoRA dropout | 0.05 |
| Trainable modules | all-linear |
| Adapter file size | ~102 MB (finetune-artifact-adapter_brazilian_crypto.tgz) |

## Other details

No pruning or quantization applied. Adapter trained in full precision via Adaption AutoScientist infrastructure.

---

# Data Overview

## Training data

**Dataset:** [Fernandosr85/adaption-brazilian-crypto-compliance](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/adaption-brazilian-crypto-compliance)

19 instruction/response pairs in JSONL chat format. Each example contains a compliance scenario as instruction and a structured JSON assessment as response. Data sources:

- 11 examples derived from pipeline-generated reports (RegTech BR RAG + Claude Sonnet 4.6)
- 8 synthetic examples covering additional regulatory scenarios

Dataset was remastered by Adaption's Adaptive Data pipeline, achieving **Grade A** with **+6.7% quality improvement**.

**Regulatory coverage:**

| Scenario | Authority | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| PSAV without BCB authorization | BCB | HIGH |
| No asset segregation | BCB | HIGH |
| KYC only above R$100k | BCB + COAF | HIGH |
| No AML/CFT officer | BCB + COAF | HIGH |
| USDT FX reporting omitted | BCB | HIGH |
| Revenue/voting token public offering | CVM | HIGH |
| RWA tokenization without CVM registration | CVM | HIGH |
| PEP without enhanced due diligence | COAF + BCB | HIGH |
| Fully compliant PSAV | BCB + COAF | LOW |
| Lei 14.478/2022 framework | Federal | LOW |
| Utility token (non-security) | CVM | REQUIRES_REVIEW |

## Demographic groups

Not applicable. Dataset covers regulatory compliance scenarios for Virtual Asset Service Providers (PSAVs) under Brazilian law, not demographic data.

## Evaluation data

No explicit train/test split given the small dataset size (19 examples). Evaluation was performed by Adaption AutoScientist on held-out internal test sets per category.

---

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Adapted model win rate | **63%** |
| Base model win rate | 37% |
| Relative improvement | +70% over base model |
| Initial train loss | 1.601 |
| Final validation loss | 0.747 |
| Loss reduction | −53% |
| Dataset quality grade | A (+6.7% improvement) |

The adapted model outperforms the base model with **63% win rate vs 37%** on Adaption's held-out legal compliance evaluation set.

## Subgroup evaluation results

Evaluation was performed across BCB, CVM, and COAF regulatory scenarios. No disaggregated subgroup analysis beyond regulatory authority category.

## Fairness

Not applicable for this regulatory compliance task. The model evaluates legal compliance of crypto asset service providers against Brazilian law, with no demographic or protected group variables.

## Usage limitations

- Fine-tuned on Brazilian crypto asset regulation as of June 2026. Regulation changes may not be reflected.
- Small training set (19 examples) — performance on highly specific or novel regulatory scenarios may be limited.
- Outputs must be reviewed by qualified legal and compliance professionals before any operational or regulatory decision.
- Not validated under OAB, BCB, CVM, or COAF frameworks.

## Ethics

This model was developed for regulatory research and compliance screening. Outputs are clearly labeled as experimental and not legal advice. No personally identifiable information was used in training. The dataset covers institutional compliance scenarios only.

---

## Credits

- **Fine-tuning platform:** [Adaption](https://adaptionlabs.ai) — AutoScientist & Adaptive Data
- **Challenge:** [AutoScientist Challenge 2026](https://adaptionlabs.ai/blog/autoscientist-challenge)
- **HuggingFace model:** [Fernandosr85/regtech-br-legal-adapter](https://huggingface.co/Fernandosr85/regtech-br-legal-adapter)
- **Demo Space:** [Fernandosr85/regtech-br](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Fernandosr85/regtech-br)
- **Author:** Fernando Rodrigues · [Kaggle: fernandosr85](https://www.kaggle.com/fernandosr85)

# Lightweight SMS Spam Classifier

## Model Overview

This project provides a tiny scikit-learn text classification model for identifying synthetic SMS messages as `ham` or `spam`. It uses a complete scikit-learn `Pipeline` with TF-IDF vectorization and Logistic Regression.

The model is intentionally small and simple so it can support Kaggle Models badge completion without heavy local training or large dependencies.

## Intended Use

Use this model for Kaggle Models publishing practice, beginner-friendly text classification demos, and testing Kaggle Model artifacts, variations, documentation, tags, links, and API access.

Do not use this model for production spam filtering, security-critical fraud or phishing detection, or evaluation of real-world messaging systems.

## Dataset

Training data: `Tiny Synthetic SMS Spam Dataset`

The dataset contains 100 synthetic SMS-style messages with `text` and `label` columns. Labels are `ham` and `spam`.

## Training Procedure

The training notebook reads the CSV dataset, splits it into train/test partitions with `random_state=42`, trains a scikit-learn pipeline, evaluates the model, and saves the complete pipeline with `joblib`.

Pipeline: `TfidfVectorizer` plus `LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, class_weight="balanced")`.

## Evaluation

Metrics are stored in `metrics.json` for each artifact upload.

| Version | Description |
|---|---|
| v1 | Unigram TF-IDF + Logistic Regression baseline |
| v2 | Unigram/bigram TF-IDF + Logistic Regression variation |

## Limitations

The dataset is tiny and synthetic. The model may overfit simple keyword patterns and is not robust to modern phishing, adversarial text, or multilingual messages. Evaluation is for workflow demonstration, not real-world performance claims.

## How to Use

```python
import joblib

model = joblib.load("/kaggle/input/lightweight-sms-spam-classifier/ScikitLearn/tfidf-logreg/1/model.joblib")
messages = ["Can you call me after lunch?", "Congratulations claim your free cash prize now"]
predictions = model.predict(messages)
print(predictions)
```

Adjust the `/kaggle/input/...` path to match the model version path shown in Kaggle.

## Tags

Recommended Kaggle tags: `nlp`, `classification`, `text-classification`, `scikit-learn`, `beginner`, `logistic-regression`. Verify supported tags in the current Kaggle UI.

## Linked Resources

Published resource links:

- Dataset: `https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sateasinpedas/tiny-synthetic-sms-spam-dataset`
- Training notebook: `https://www.kaggle.com/code/sateasinpedas/01-train-spam-classifier`
- Inference notebook: `https://www.kaggle.com/code/sateasinpedas/02-inference-from-kaggle-model`
- Model: `https://www.kaggle.com/models/sateasinpedas/lightweight-sms-spam-classifier`

## Version History

- v1: Baseline unigram TF-IDF + Logistic Regression pipeline.
- v2: Bigram-enabled TF-IDF + Logistic Regression variation/version.
